Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::What is a package?}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Packages prevent name conflicts (e.g., having java.util.Date and java.sql.Date coexist) and organize code into logical units. They also enforce encapsulation via package-private access.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Create package}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Declared using the package keyword as the first statement. Gotcha: Placing package after imports or class definitions causes compile-time errors. The folder structure must match the package path.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Import package}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Supports single type import and wildcard import. Wildcard imports are NOT recursive; they only import classes directly in that package, not sub-packages.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::import static}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Imports static members (variables or methods) of a class so they can be referenced directly. Gotcha: Writing static import instead of import static is a compile-time error.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Default package}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Classes in the default package cannot be imported or accessed by classes in named packages. Placed in default package if package statement is missing.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Package naming convention}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Uses lowercase words separated by dots (e.g., com.company.project.module). Lowercase is used to prevent naming conflicts with classes.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Access between packages}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Visibility: public (anywhere), protected (subclasses and same package), package-private (same package only), and private (class only).

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Classpath}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Tells JVM/compiler where to search for compiled classes and JAR files. Specified via -cp, -classpath, or CLASSPATH.

Text: In Package and Access Control, {{c1::Basic module path}} is a concept you should define, apply, and connect to common mistakes.
Extra: Java 9+ alternative (--module-path or -p) specifying directories containing modular JARs or compiled modules. Enforces strong encapsulation defined in module-info.java.
